Chapter 7: The Rituals That Sustain Us.
Have you ever noticed how the little things you do every day—those routines that seem almost automatic—can actually help you feel grounded when life gets a bit unpredictable? For these women, it was the simple, repeated actions that really anchored them. Think about that first cup of coffee in the morning, setting the table for dinner, or washing paintbrushes at the end of a creative session. These small rituals became touchstones—a way to remember what truly matters.
Picture this: it’s a chilly winter evening, snow quietly drifting outside. The women gather close friends for a cozy meal. Nothing fancy, just soup bubbling on the stove, bread warming in the oven, and a salad bursting with citrus. The table’s set with mismatched plates and flickering candles, the room alive with laughter, the gentle clink of glasses, and easy conversation. As they pass bread, pour wine, and swap stories, they realize it’s these rituals—the simple acts shared around a table—that create real warmth and a deep sense of belonging, something that lingers long after the plates are cleared.
In the studio, rituals show up differently. There’s the careful setup of materials, a quiet pause before starting, and the subtle way sunlight shifts across the room as hours pass. These routines aren’t just habits—they’re ways to mark time, to carve out space for focus and reflection. And even on days when inspiration feels miles away, just showing up—mixing paint or even chopping vegetables—becomes its own reward.
Of course, there are days when rituals feel like a burden. When work and family pull you in every direction, and it’s tough to make space for creativity. But somehow, these women always find a way to hold onto what matters. Maybe it’s a quick sketch squeezed in during a lunch break, or a shared pot of tea right in the middle of the chaos. These tiny acts become lifelines—a reminder that beauty and meaning can always be found in the midst of everyday life.
Most of us brush off ritual as just routine, don’t we? But in these kitchens and studios, it’s clear: rituals are actually the scaffolding of a creative life. They’re the structure that lets us feel safe enough to take risks, to try something new. That familiar repetition gives us a sense of security—a foundation we can build on.
Over time, these women learned to treasure their rituals, to see them not as restrictions, but as true gifts. The kitchen and the studio became sanctuaries—places to set the world aside, even if just for a moment. In the end, it’s these daily acts of care and attention that sustain us. They make the work possible. They give shape and meaning to our days—and remind us that even the smallest moments can carry the deepest significance.
